entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Ebola death toll in DRC surges to at least 930 as outbreak continues spread. *Ebola is spreading faster than any previous outbreak in DRC, with 37 new deaths recorded over just 24 hours at the weekend.*. The death toll from the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen to at least 930 and the virus appears to be spreading faster. The health ministry said on Monday that the number of confirmed cases had reached at least 2,344. That is total confirmed total as of Saturday with 37 deaths recorded in just 24 hours from Friday – one of the highest daily increases recorded since the Ebola outbreak was first declared in the DRC on May 15. The World Health Organization (WHO) warned last week that Ebola is spreading in the DRC faster than in any previous outbreak. This time, it took only two months to reach 2,000 confirmed cases, and the ⁠⁠WHO said the ⁠⁠true tally could be at least double that.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Thousands sickened by lettuce in US: what may be lurking in your salad bowl? - Ynetnews
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: ## A Cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce highlights the importance of handling leafy greens safely at home; how can you reduce infection risk, and which common mistakes allow bacteria to thrive in your refrigerator? Thousands of people in the United States have fallen ill in recent months with a parasitic infection of the digestive system. Now, after weeks of epidemiological investigation, health authorities have identified the source of the outbreak: chopped iceberg lettuce grown in Mexico and supplied to Taco Bell locations in five U.S. states. How did the parasite spread, and what does it mean for the vegetable drawer in your refrigerator and the way you handle leafy greens? An investigation by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration led to a single supplier of iceberg lettuce from Mexico. The Cyclospora outbreak in the United States illustrates that even vegetables considered healthy and safe can become contaminated at various stages along the way from the field to the plate.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Flood-hit Agriculture Needs Urgent Climate Action - daily-sun.com
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Bangladesh’s agriculture is currently facing one of the most severe consequences of climate change. According to the latest data from the Ministry of Agriculture, floods have affected 43 districts across the country, damaging crops on 114,723 hectares of land. Of this, 107,845 hectares-- nearly 90 per cent of the total affected area-- are located in 16 districts. The worst-affected crops are Aus rice, Aman seedbeds and seasonal vegetables. Approximately 79,500 hectares of Aus rice, 10,504 hectares of Aman seedbeds, and 17,800 hectares of seasonal vegetables have been damaged. According to preliminary information from the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Cumilla, crops on 19,899 hectares have been affected in Cumilla district alone. Of these, 19,477 hectares were standing crops, while crops on 2,671 hectares have already been damaged. A crop-wise assessment shows that transplanted Aman rice has suffered the largest overall impact, with 66 hectares damaged out of 16,200 hectares cultivated. A comprehensive recovery of agriculture, fisheries, and livestock is essential for restoring the rural economy.
